subject: Agriculture
title: Fishing and Ocean Depletion
description: A quick win: understand Fishing and Ocean Depletion.

hook.text: 34% of global fish stocks are overfished. The ocean's abundance was never infinite—we're proving it.

buildup.text: Industrial trawlers scrape the ocean floor, catching everything—target species and bycatch alike.

discovery.text: Cod stocks off Newfoundland collapsed in 1992 after decades of overfishing. Thirty years later, they haven't recovered.

twist.text: Aquaculture now provides more fish than wild catch. But farmed fish eat wild fish—it doesn't always reduce pressure.

climax.text: Well-managed fisheries can be sustainable. Iceland and New Zealand prove it—but most fisheries lack governance.

punchline.text: The ocean can feed us forever—only if we stop taking more than it can give.

quiz.question: What percentage of global fish stocks are currently overfished?

details.summary: Global fishing has pushed many marine species to the brink of collapse. This topic covers overfishing, illegal fishing, bycatch, and how fisheries management must evolve to sustain ocean ecosystems and the billions of people who depend on seafood.
details.whyItMatters: Over 3 billion people depend on fish for essential protein. One-third of global fish stocks are already overfished, threatening both marine ecosystems and human food security.
takeaways: About 34% of the world's fish stocks are overfished beyond sustainable levels
Illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing accounts for up to $23 billion annually
Science-based catch limits have successfully restored depleted stocks in some regions

faq.question: Why is overfishing a serious problem for global food security?
faq.answer: Overfishing depletes fish populations faster than they can reproduce, threatening collapse of species that provide essential protein for over 3 billion people. It also disrupts marine ecosystems on which healthy fisheries depend.

faq.question: What solutions can help restore overfished stocks?
faq.answer: Effective solutions include science-based catch quotas, marine protected areas, eliminating harmful fishing subsidies, combating illegal fishing with satellite monitoring, and supporting aquaculture as a complementary protein source.
